title: Choose the package page's structure
question: Third hand, built for your steer: versions on every commit, tens of thousands a day. Feature parity with npm, Artifactory, Nexus and GitHub Packages is assumed; this picks the composition.

options.label: Query console
options.lineage: a log explorer's query bar and facets, pointed at versions
options.thesis: Treat versions as data: one query over every version, facet counts beside it, bulk actions, built for tens of thousands a day.
options.viewport: Header and pull command; a query bar (source:orbit/web branch:main since:24h) with saved views like Released and Today; a publish-rate strip over a virtualized version table; facet counts (source, branch, status, tag) on the right; select rows to tag, yank or delete.
options.risk: Cold at first glance unless the default views answer the common questions before anyone types.

regions.label: versions (virtualized): version · tags · source@commit · run · age

options.label: Channels
options.thesis: Separate noise from signal: per-commit builds flow into channels by branch or source, each a row with its cadence, latest build and tags.
options.viewport: Header and pull command; released tags float in a strip at the top; below, one row per channel (main, release/*, feature branches) with a cadence sparkline, builds today, latest version with its commit and CI status; expanding a row opens that channel's build stream.
options.risk: Builds without branch information, like manual uploads, collect in one catch-all channel.

options.label: Retention first
options.lineage: a storage console that leads with policy
options.thesis: At this volume the real question is what to keep: versions sorted into kept, recent and prunable, with storage and policy up front.
options.viewport: Header; a storage bar split into kept (tagged or released), recent and prunable; retention rules beside a live preview of what the next sweep removes; version lists per bucket below.
options.risk: Leads with housekeeping, the opposite of what most visits want, which is finding a version.
